key_decisions.decision: Passive English leaves unnamed handlers unspecified; Eleazar supervises outside camp rather than necessarily slaughtering himself.
Preserves every burned component, including blood and dung, and supervision by sight.
Keeps permission to return before evening distinct from continuing ritual impurity.
Retains clean male collector and outside storage; contextual purification rendering of hattat is explained rather than forced into ordinary altar sacrifice.
Follows Hebrew clause division; note explains possible attachment of seventh day to purification and verse 19’s explicit two sprinklings.
Keeps sanctuary defilement, severe cut-off consequence and repeated continuing impurity without specifying an unstated execution mechanism.
Renders living water as fresh, with source image noted; preserves ashes and container rather than a running-water bath.
Makes changed subject of washing explicit and retains both sprinkling days plus evening completion.
Keeps repeated sanction and sanctuary wording rather than deleting it as redundant.
Preserves distinct sprinkler-washing and toucher-evening clauses without adding an unstated evening penalty to the sprinkler.
